scenes.tts: Stretched dishes show more tracked divisions. What else, besides stretch, changed in those dishes? Chapter one locked three things: the prediction, endpoint and independent unit. A control is how you find out.
scenes.visual: Open on chapter 1's dark bench. The same large grey culture dish with blue epithelial-cell cartoons sits centre; four white outward arrows mark schematic biaxial stretch. A gold tracked path ends in two daughter cells beside the dish. Gold question marks immediately rise toward the stretch device, medium bottle and microscope. As chapter 1 is recalled, those candidates dim and the three closed gold locks ('prediction', 'endpoint', 'independent unit') descend above the dish. Never show more than six objects at once. Label the cells and stretch picture 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Stretched dishes show more tracked divisions. What else, besides stretch, changed in those dishes? Chapter one locked three things: the prediction, endpoint and independent unit. A control is how you find out.

scenes.visual: Keep the bench dimly visible. Bring in the title 'Ruling Out the Dull Explanations' for under 2 seconds. As it fades, a second, unstretched dish slides in on the left as a twin of the stretched dish, both outlined in blue. The question marks keep drifting.

scenes.tts: Look at what the stretched dish went through. Someone assembled the device, mounted it and carried it to the microscope. If the control dish skipped those steps, stretch now includes every handling difference. So unstretched devices are assembled, mounted and imaged identically.
scenes.visual: Animate the stretched dish's journey as a short gold trail: a wrench icon 'assemble', a clamp icon 'mount', a microscope icon 'image'. The left dish first sits still with no trail, and a red gap marker appears between the two dishes labelled 'handling'. Then the left dish travels the same trail step for step, the gap marker shrinks to nothing, and a first row 'handling: matched' appears in a two-column comparison table beneath the dishes.
scenes.narration: Look at what the stretched dish went through. Someone assembled the device, mounted it and carried it to the microscope. If the control dish skipped those steps, stretch now includes every handling difference. So unstretched devices are assembled, mounted and imaged identically.

scenes.tts: The medium raises the same problem. Wnt three A medium comes from mouse L cells engineered to make Wnt three A. The matched control is medium from the parental L cells, prepared the same way. Even that cannot promise Wnt three A is the only difference.
scenes.caption: The medium raises the same problem. Wnt3A medium comes from mouse L cells engineered to make Wnt3A. The matched control is medium from the parental L cells, prepared the same way. Even that cannot promise Wnt3A is the only difference.
scenes.visual: Two medium bottles roll in from the top, each fed by a small cartoon cell labelled 'L cell'. One cell carries a gold block labelled 'Wnt3A'; the other is plain, labelled 'parental L cell'. Each bottle pours into one dish. Add the table row 'medium: matched preparation'. Then differently shaped faint grey specks labelled 'other differences?' appear in the two bottles and pulse, to show that identical composition is not guaranteed.
scenes.narration: The medium raises the same problem. Wnt3A medium comes from mouse L cells engineered to make Wnt3A. The matched control is medium from the parental L cells, prepared the same way. Even that cannot promise Wnt3A is the only difference.

scenes.tts: So add a readout of the pathway itself. Top-d-G-F-P is a short-lived green reporter driven by beta-catenin-responsive sites. Its signal asks whether the Wnt medium engaged beta-catenin-dependent transcription in these cells. If it stays flat, the medium may not have done its job.
scenes.caption: So add a readout of the pathway itself. TOPdGFP is a short-lived green reporter driven by beta-catenin-responsive sites. Its signal asks whether the Wnt medium engaged beta-catenin-dependent transcription in these cells. If it stays flat, the medium may not have done its job.
scenes.visual: Zoom into one cell of the Wnt3A dish. Inside the nucleus, a labelled block 'beta-catenin' joins a block 'TCF' on a plain promoter bar marked 'responsive sites'; do not draw a DNA helix or any molecular structure. A gauge labelled 'TOPdGFP signal' beside the nucleus rises slowly. In an inset cell from the control-medium dish, the same gauge stays low. Mark both gauges 'schematic'. Use blocks, a plain bar and gauges only.
scenes.narration: So add a readout of the pathway itself. TOPdGFP is a short-lived green reporter driven by beta-catenin-responsive sites. Its signal asks whether the Wnt medium engaged beta-catenin-dependent transcription in these cells. If it stays flat, the medium may not have done its job.

scenes.tts: Each of these follows one rule. A good control matches the treatment in every step except the one being tested. Without that match, the dull explanation and the interesting one predict the same result. Then a difference between them can point to that step.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the twin dishes and their comparison table. A gold bracket wraps every matched row; a single unmatched row, 'stretch: yes / no', glows white between the two dishes. A gold arrow runs from that row to the tracked-division path. The question marks around the bench dim one by one as each matched row lights.
scenes.narration: Each of these follows one rule. A good control matches the treatment in every step except the one being tested. Without that match, the dull explanation and the interesting one predict the same result. Then a difference between them can point to that step.

scenes.tts: A drug control gets the vehicle, the drug's solvent without drug, at the same concentration. Whoever scores the cells fixes positivity thresholds before analysis and scores blind to condition. Otherwise expectations can slip into the counts, one borderline cell at a time.
scenes.visual: A pipette adds a teal drop labelled 'drug + solvent' to the right dish and a clear drop labelled 'solvent only' to the left; row 'vehicle: matched' appears. Then a cartoon scorer at the microscope gets a blindfold; dish labels flip to 'A' and 'B'. A threshold line labelled 'fixed in advance' locks onto a green-intensity bar before any cells are scored. Row 'scoring: blind' appears.
scenes.narration: A drug control gets the vehicle, the drug's solvent without drug, at the same concentration. Whoever scores the cells fixes positivity thresholds before analysis and scores blind to condition. Otherwise expectations can slip into the counts, one borderline cell at a time.

scenes.tts: Stretch itself must be checked. Measure the strain the cells actually feel, and analyze only the strained region. In the twenty sixteen study, two biaxial devices reached about eight point five and fifteen percent. Those results should not be merged. Each device is its own condition.
scenes.caption: Stretch itself must be checked. Measure the strain the cells actually feel, and analyze only the strained region. In the 2016 study, two biaxial devices reached about 8.5% and 15%. Those results should not be merged. Each device is its own condition.
scenes.visual: The stretched dish becomes a membrane with a square grid drawn on it. In the central strained region, every square expands in both directions while remaining square; the surrounding grid stays unchanged. Four outward arrows make the biaxial direction explicit, and a gold outline marks 'analyzed strained region'. Beside it, two device cards show bars labelled 'live imager: about 8.5%' and 'strain array: about 15%' maximum strain, drawn to scale. A red 'do not merge' line separates the two bars. Row 'strain: measured' appears. Mark the grid 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Stretch itself must be checked. Measure the strain the cells actually feel, and analyze only the strained region. In the 2016 study, two biaxial devices reached about 8.5% and 15%. Those results should not be merged. Each device is its own condition.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Suppose stretched cells stall, and you suspect DNA damage. You stain for a damage marker, and it stays blank. Does that blank marker show there was no damage?
scenes.visual: A stretched cell sits in green with a pause sign beside it. A schematic fluorescence field labelled 'DNA-damage marker' appears beside the dish and stays blank. A bright question card reads 'Blank marker = no damage?' Cells pulse slowly; no answer appears. Do not draw a dipstick or imply that the stain is a test-strip assay.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Suppose stretched cells stall, and you suspect DNA damage. You stain for a damage marker, and it stays blank. Does that blank marker show there was no damage?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card fully visible. The blank test strip sways gently and the stalled green cell keeps pulsing. No check mark or answer highlight appears.

scenes.tts: Only if the assay could have seen damage. Benham-Pyle and colleagues ran methyl methanesulfonate, a DNA-damaging chemical, as a positive control. It shows the assay detects damage when damage is present. Even then, one missing marker cannot rule out every kind of damage.
scenes.visual: A third dish slides in, labelled 'positive control: MMS'. A matched schematic fluorescence field from it shows a bright damage-marker signal beside the blank field from the stretched dish. A bracket from the bright positive-control field reads 'assay detects this marker'. Then faint grey cards labelled 'other damage types?' appear behind the two fields, untested, to show the limit. Row 'positive control: run' appears in the table.
scenes.narration: Only if the assay could have seen damage. Benham-Pyle and colleagues ran methyl methanesulfonate, a DNA-damaging chemical, as a positive control. It shows the assay detects damage when damage is present. Even then, one missing marker cannot rule out every kind of damage.

scenes.tts: Return to the stretched dish and its unstretched twin. They share the handling, medium, vehicle and blinded scorer. The strain itself was measured. Only the stretch differs. Now a difference in tracked divisions can point to stretch, for the period watched.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the twin dishes at full height with chapter 1's three gold locks above them. The comparison table compresses into a gold band joining the dishes for matched handling, medium, vehicle and blinded scoring. A separate measurement badge sits beside the only white gap, 'stretch: measured versus zero'. The gold question marks that opened the chapter turn into check marks one by one. A small clock icon labelled 'period watched' sits beside the tracked-division path.
scenes.narration: Return to the stretched dish and its unstretched twin. They share the handling, medium, vehicle and blinded scorer. The strain itself was measured. Only the stretch differs. Now a difference in tracked divisions can point to stretch, for the period watched.

scenes.visual: End card on the dark ground with the site's mascot waving above the line 'A good control differs from the treatment in one step only.' High-contrast white, centred, 11 words.
